messages.text: How many chips does the nexus S1 have?
Read the nexus s1 10th s page

Four, Nicholas. The listing says the Nexus S1 runs 4× BM1373 ASIC chips for about 10 TH/s at around 150 W, which works out to roughly 15 J/TH.

Is this for comparing it against your Octaxes, or for something else?

Nicholas, on paper they're close. The S1 does about 10 TH/s at 150 W, around 15 J/TH, on 4 BM1373 chips. Our NerdOctaxe listing gives 9.4 TH/s at stock and up to 12 TH/s overclocked, drawing 160 to 220 W. The BSB version lists 12 TH/s at about 160 W, roughly 13.3 J/TH. Neither Octaxe listing says how many chips or which ones.

So an S1 wouldn't really be an upgrade on your Octaxes. It's the same hashrate in a smaller box. For a real step up, it's still the Magic M. or a second B30.
I was thinking about replacing my current NerQaxe++ rev 7 with a few nexus S1s

I'd steer you away from that, Nicholas. Three S1s cost $2,097 for about 30 TH/s. One Magic M. 40T is $799 for 40 TH/s, and one B30 is $899 for 30 TH/s. Both are pre-orders. The Magic M. ships December 21, 2026 and the B30 ships November 30, 2026. The US S1 also isn't orderable right now.

We don't carry the Rev 7, so I can't give you its specs from our side. What hashrate and wattage does yours show on the dashboard?

That's a good unit, Nicholas. 7.5 TH/s at 125 W works out to about 16.7 J/TH. The S1 is listed at about 15 J/TH, so a swap would get you roughly 2.5 TH/s more per unit for $699 each. That's a lot of money for a small gain.

Your B30 lands this month at 30 TH/s. That's four Rev 7s' worth in one box. I'd keep the Rev 7 running next to it and add the Magic M. if you want more.
Glad it helped, Nicholas. Once the B30 is running, tell me what the dashboard shows next to the Rev 7. That'll make it easy to decide whether a Magic M. is worth adding.
